note: Seeded wordiness the concise brief names: throat-clearing openings, filler and empty qualifiers, redundant pairs, wordy phrases, nouns made from verbs, needless passive voice, and repeated points. The rest of each document is kept tight so extra findings are easy to judge; pool-closure-notice-strong.md is a decoy written in already tight prose.

office-move-update.md.quote: I just wanted to take a quick moment to reach out to all of you
office-move-update.md.issue: A throat-clearing opening paragraph that says nothing; cut it and start with the moving date.

office-move-update.md.quote: It has been decided by the partners that we will move
office-move-update.md.issue: Needless passive voice; "The partners have decided we will move" or simply "We move" says it in fewer words.

office-move-update.md.quote: In order to keep disruption to a minimum
office-move-update.md.issue: Wordy phrase: "In order to" can be "To" (and "keep disruption to a minimum" can be "minimize disruption").
Empty qualifiers ("really very"); "bright" or "very bright" is enough.

office-move-update.md.quote: Due to the fact that the lease
office-move-update.md.issue: Wordy phrase: "Due to the fact that" can be "Because".

office-move-update.md.quote: We will make a final decision on the seating plan once the partners have given consideration to the feedback from the survey.
office-move-update.md.issue: Nouns made from verbs ("make a final decision", "given consideration to"); "We will settle the seating plan once the partners have considered the survey feedback."

office-move-update.md.quote: To sum up and remind everyone once again
office-move-update.md.issue: The closing section repeats the dates, times and to-do list already given above; cut it or reduce it to one line.

volunteer-portal-howto.md.quote: Basically, this guide is for new volunteers
At this point in time, the portal
volunteer-portal-howto.md.issue: Wordy phrase: "At this point in time" can be cut or replaced with "now".

volunteer-portal-howto.md.quote: Text alerts are absolutely essential for volunteers.
Shift changes are sent by text message and are not sent by email.
volunteer-portal-howto.md.issue: Wordy and repetitive; "Shift changes go out by text, not email."
Redundant pair: "free" and "available" mean the same here.

volunteer-portal-howto.md.quote: carries out a review of everyone's availability every Monday and makes an assignment of shifts by Wednesday
volunteer-portal-howto.md.issue: Nouns made from verbs ("carries out a review of", "makes an assignment of"); "reviews everyone's availability every Monday and assigns shifts by Wednesday".

volunteer-portal-howto.md.quote: The agreement is required to be read and signed by all volunteers before their first shift.
volunteer-portal-howto.md.issue: Needless passive voice; "Read and sign the agreement before your first shift."

volunteer-portal-howto.md.quote: Note that it is important to remember that your account is personal.
volunteer-portal-howto.md.issue: The paragraph opens with throat-clearing and then says the account is personal a second time; it can be one short sentence.

support-quarterly-report.md.issue: Wordy phrase: "a large number of" can be "many".
Noun made from a verb; "We believe" is shorter.

support-quarterly-report.md.quote: Satisfaction was measured by a short survey that was sent after each ticket was closed, and the average score was found to be 4.3 out of 5.
support-quarterly-report.md.issue: A chain of needless passives; "Customers rated us 4.3 out of 5 on the survey sent after each closed ticket."

support-quarterly-report.md.quote: At the end of the day, what we really need to do going forward is basically make sure that weekend coverage gets improved.
support-quarterly-report.md.issue: A sentence of filler ("At the end of the day", "really", "going forward", "basically"); "We need better weekend coverage."
Noun made from a verb; "study whether" or "test whether".

support-quarterly-report.md.quote: In summary, to go over the main points of this report once more
support-quarterly-report.md.issue: The closing summary repeats the overview at the top of this short report point for point; cut it.
